label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 2 · Question 12
knowledgePattern: Count distinct trigonometric roots across parameter boundary cases
solution:
Factor to sinx(cos2x−p2)=0. The sine factor always gives x=0,π,2π.

If p=0, cosx=0 adds π/2,3π/2, so n=5. If 0<|p|<1, the two nonzero levels cosx=±|p| contribute four new roots, so n=7.

If |p|=1, the cosine roots are already among the three sine roots; if |p|>1, no cosine roots are possible. Both cases give n=3.

I is false, for example at p=1 (also at p=−1). II is true, because n=7 requires 0<|p|<1, which implies −1<p<1. II only: answer C.

hints.title: Factor without dividing
hints.body: Move all terms to one side and extract the common trigonometric factor.
hints.recap: Factoring retains the solutions that division by a zero-capable trigonometric factor can lose.

recall.reminder: Factoring retains the solutions that division by a zero-capable trigonometric factor can lose.

hints.title: Separate the parameter cases
hints.body: Use the range of cosine and separate zero levels, boundary levels and levels strictly between the boundaries. Count distinct roots on the closed interval.
hints.recap: Root counts require separate boundary cases and deduplication where branches meet.
hints.pitfall: The endpoints are included, and a root shared by two factors is still one distinct root.
hints.pause: Build a short table of the root count against the parameter cases, then test the two implications.
